paper.title: Evolution of microstructure, texture and mechanical properties of Fe–30Mn–11Al–1.2C low-density steel during cold rolling
paper.paper_scope: Systematic investigation of the evolution of microstructure, texture and mechanical properties of a single Fe–30Mn–11Al–1.2C (wt%) austenitic low-density steel during cold rolling up to 90% thickness reduction, with cold rolling reduction as the only process variable.

alloys.description: A high Mn–Al–C austenitic low-density steel fabricated by vacuum induction melting, then soaked at 1250 °C for 12 h and hot-forged into 60 mm diameter bars (finish forging temperature 900 °C). The as-quenched microstructure consists of austenite with uniformly distributed nano-sized κ'-carbides; used to study cold-rolling induced microstructure, texture and property evolution.
alloys.alloys_notes: Nominal composition given as Fe–30Mn–11Al–1.2C (wt%). The stacking fault energy (SFE) of the steel was estimated as ~108 mJ/m² and the Burgers vector of a partial dislocation as 0.146 nm. The as-quenched phase constituent was austenite plus κ'-carbides, with a grain size (including twins) of ~70 μm and an almost random initial texture.

source.reason: The paper investigates a single alloy: a high Mn–Al–C austenitic low-density steel whose nominal component is reported as Fe–30Mn–11Al–1.2C (wt%), fabricated by vacuum induction melting and processed into bars/sheets.

unmapped_findings: The stacking fault energy (SFE) of the steel was estimated as ~108 mJ/m² and the Burgers vector for a partial dislocation as 0.146 nm; the calculated critical shear stress for deformation twinning is ~1.48 GPa, much higher than the maximum resolved shear stress ~0.75 GPa.
The steel was fabricated by vacuum induction melting, soaked at 1250 °C for 12 h and hot-forged into 60 mm diameter bars with a finish forging temperature of 900 °C.
The as-quenched microstructure consists of austenite and uniformly distributed nano-sized κ'-carbides formed via spinodal decomposition during quenching; the grain size (including twins) is ~70 μm.
With increasing cold rolling reduction the yield strength rises to ~2.0 GPa after 90% reduction (~3.5 times the as-quenched value) while uniform elongation decreases (strength-ductility trade-off).

The deformation substructure evolution follows the sequence Taylor lattice → microbands → nano-twins → shear bands → dislocation cells/tangles; twinning occurred at low resolved shear stress despite the high SFE.

The overall rolling texture is weak, characterized by a transition from 'copper-type' to 'brass-type' texture at 50% cold rolling reduction, attributed to dislocation planar glide and deformation twinning.
